name: Felwood
summary: Felwood remains in the grip of corruption between Ashenvale and Mount Hyjal. Once a paradise tended by night elves, it was poisoned by demonic magic during the Third War. Satyrs, twisted beasts, and ancients roam its depths as the Cenarion Circle and Alliance and Horde outposts work to cleanse it.

sections.title: A Paradise Befouled
sections.body:
Before the Third War, clear streams ran beneath singing birds, and ancient protectors guarded the peaceful groves. Then the dreadlord Tichondrius and the Burning Legion brought that peace to an end. Before their assault on Mount Hyjal, they used the Skull of Gul'dan to poison northern Kalimdor. Its sorcery blackened the forest floor and turned it to mire.

Illidan Stormrage later slew Tichondrius and consumed the artifact's essence. Yet the fel corruption remained. Treants and ancients rotted within, rivers boiled with bile, and the forest's beasts fell into cannibalistic madness.

sections.title: The War for Cleansing
sections.body:
The work of healing Felwood is slow. On its southern border, the Cenarion Circle fights the blight from the Emerald Sanctuary. Its druids tend poisoned songflowers and night dragon bulbs, and give wanderers Cenarion beacons and cleansing salves.

The night elves hold Talonbranch Glade in the north, while the Horde keeps Bloodvenom Post. Both footholds stand amid a deadly wilderness where nature has turned against mortal flesh.

sections.title: The Shadow in Jaedenar
sections.body:
Cultists still nurture Felwood's fel taint. In the underground labyrinth of Jaedenar and Shadow Hold, remnants of the Shadow Council perform foul rituals under Lord Banehollow's direction. They are allied with deceitful satyrs who desecrate ancient moonwells.

The warlocks draw upon the forest's agony and summon demonic reinforcements. Felwood cannot be redeemed while the council remains rooted here.

faq.answer: During the Third War, the dreadlord Tichondrius used the demonic Skull of Gul'dan to corrupt the forest. The Legion sought to weaken the night elves' defenses before its march on Mount Hyjal. Wildlife, water, and ancients were blighted.

faq.q: Can the corrupted plants in the forest be cleansed?
faq.answer: Yes. Druids of the Cenarion Circle provide salves brewed from collected fel taints and mineral residues. Apply them to songflowers, whiplash tubers, and night dragons to purge their corruption and gain restorative fruit and blessings.

The clandestine Shadow Council, a sect of mortal warlocks and demon worshippers, controls Jaedenar. From the underground caverns of Shadow Hold, the dreadlord Lord Banehollow oversees their rituals and commands the satyrs in the region.

faq.q: Are the furbolgs in Felwood hostile?
faq.answer: Most are hostile. The Deadwood tribes have wholly succumbed to demonic corruption and fel madness. The Timbermaw hold the northern tunnel network and remain uncorrupted, but distrust outsiders until they prove friendly.

faq.q: How do you get to Moonglade or Winterspring through Felwood?
faq.answer: The road north leads into Timbermaw Hold, a fortified cavern complex. The uncorrupted Timbermaw furbolgs control the tunnels from Felwood to Moonglade and Winterspring. You must earn their trust or fight your way through.

faq.q: Why do the corrupted ancients attack night elves?
faq.answer: Demonic magic warped and poisoned the once-noble ancients and treants. Eternal agony has shattered their minds, and they resent the night elves, whom they believe abandoned them to the Burning Legion.

angles.text: For the Cenarion Circle, Felwood is a profound tragedy. As a druid, you dedicate your life to cleansing its blighted plants and calming maddened nature spirits.
As a kaldorei, you know the desecration of these ancient woods brings immense grief and shame. Your people failed to protect them from the Legion's touch.
As a warlock, you find Felwood's dark tunnels and lingering demonic forces a focal point in your hunt for rival Shadow Council cultists.
As a herbalist, you can gather rare, volatile flora from Felwood's fel-soaked earth. Few places in Azeroth offer Gromsblood and Arthas' Tears.
